title: Elora green space lighting funded from existing budget
subtitle: Council backed the Ontario Food Belt bill, received transit and operations centre updates, and endorsed source protection changes.
overview: Council's most debated item was seasonal lighting for the Elora green space. Staff had sought money from the General Capital Reserve to install lights the township now owns. Council instead directed staff to use the existing 2025 operating budget and resources {{vote:m10}}, and to discuss seasonal lighting with both the Elora and Fergus BIAs {{vote:m11}}. Residents will not see a tax increase for this project.

Council also endorsed the intent of the proposed Ontario Food Belt bill after two MPPs presented it. It will ask ROMA to support the bill and will circulate the decision to Wellington County municipalities {{vote:m4}}. Council endorsed draft water quantity policy changes to the Grand River Source Protection Plan {{vote:m8}} and received reports on the transit feasibility study {{vote:m7}} and operations centre construction {{vote:m9}}.

After a closed session, council approved the Fire Rescue 2025 market compensation review {{vote:m3}}. Council also amended the parking by-law so it takes effect January 1, 2026 {{vote:m12}}. An appointment to the county accessibility committee was deferred to the next meeting.

decisions.detail: Council replaced the proposed $11,835 General Capital Reserve funding with direction for staff to use the existing 2025 operating budget and resources {{vote:m10}}.
Council directed staff to discuss seasonal lighting with both the Elora and Fergus BIAs {{vote:m11}}.
Council supported the bill's intent, will ask ROMA to support it, and will circulate the decision to Wellington County municipalities and the County.
Following a closed session, council approved the Centre Wellington Fire Rescue 2025 Market Compensation Review.
Council endorsed the draft water quantity policy amendments to the Grand River Source Protection Plan under Section 34 of the Clean Water Act.
Council passed By-law 2025-61 so the AMPS parking by-law takes effect January 1, 2026.
Council received Report IS2025-31 on the start of the transit feasibility study and the invitation to take part.
Council received Report IS2025-30 on construction progress at the operations centre, whose overall budget is $28.2 million.

debate: Two delegates opposed the lighting proposal. They argued the project was meant to be privately funded and that public money should not cover it. One raised environmental concerns about excess light, and one suggested the township-owned lights could be used elsewhere in the township.
The Elora BIA chair said the BIA would discuss funding part of the cost at its next meeting. The chair argued that lighting draws visitors and supports jobs in the slower winter months.

Several councillors opposed drawing on the capital reserve. They cited other priorities and fairness to Fergus and Bellwood. Others wanted to hear from the BIA first, and one suggested deferring the item.

Staff said the downtown beautification budget was already used up for the year. Finance staff cautioned that funds found elsewhere in the operating budget must be offset by savings. Staff said the installer needed a decision soon.

During the Food Belt presentation, the MPPs cited ongoing farmland loss and food security concerns. Council members said agriculture is a major local industry that must be balanced with growth pressure.
